title: Build tutorials v1 — recreate a repo by its decisions, in VS Code, on repo-tour's core
spec:
OBJECTIVE: a VS Code extension that turns an idea into a TUTORIAL instead of a vibecoded app — a paint-by-numbers walkthrough that teaches the DECISIONS behind why a file or repo is shaped the way it is. v1 = recreate-as-it-stands: point it at a real repo and be walked through building it, step by step, with the author's decision at every step shown against the alternatives.

WHY (Evan, verbatim): 'You see how repo-tour interprets a repo and tells you how it works? I want an app that walks me through how to code it and what kinds of decisions go into making a file or repo the way it is. Basically, a paint by numbers to create an app.' The complaint is not that code appears; it is that the reasoning never does. It is the inverse of repo-tour and shares its core — 'part of the same app'.

SUCCESS SHAPE (the 10 criteria in .autodev/specs/T-1-build-tutorials-v1.md §9): from an empty folder and a local TS/JS/Python repo, the start screen yields an ordered decision list covering every source file in dependency order, each step carrying question / options (author's marked) / why / witness / scaffold ranges; automated mode reproduces the reference byte-for-byte; scaffolded stubs parse and a filled stub passes a deterministic structural check; a tutor with the learner-vs-reference diff in context, one transcript per step; a detour that leaves the workspace untouched; skins shared with repo-tour (one CSS file → both front ends); reload-safe; a .vsix that builds; cost reported honestly. Data model complete from day one so Mode A (T-9) and divergence (T-10) are a change of defaults, not new machinery.
